title: Tenant quarantine + snapshot-fallback-by-hash and surgical hotpatch for post-upgrade config drift
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several customers experienced tenant-level failures during Private/VPC rolling upgrades where operator post-upgrade reconciliation applied stale/partial Helm value merges that caused config drift and service disruptions. This ticket implements a multi-pronged recovery: (1) automatic tenant quarantine when operator reconciliation deviates by hash-check beyond threshold, (2) snapshot-fallback-by-hash that restores the most recent consistent manifest snapshot for affected tenant(s), and (3) a surgical hotpatch release that avoids full rollback of the operator to preserve cluster-level upgrades. The initiative spans code changes in the operator, Helm preflight validators, telemetry and runbook updates, and customer communications templates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run a staged operator Helm upgrade across a multi-tenant on-prem cluster where some tenants have ephemeral externalSecret hooks
2) Inject a Helm value schema change in the upgrade that introduces a new optional top-level key; have nodeagent reconcile concurrently
3) Simulate slow APIServer responses so the operator performs a partial apply and re-enqueues reconciliation
4) Observe per-tenant CR manifests diverging: some tenants receive merged/partial values leading to invalid sidecar mounts and pod crashloops.
acceptance_criteria: When a tenant reconcile delta hash exceeds threshold X, operator marks tenant as QUARANTINED and emits telemetry event 'tenant.quarantine.triggered'
Automated snapshot-fallback restores a manifest snapshot by stable-hash within 60s for quarantined tenants and triggers a dry-run reconcile to validate restored state
Helm preflight validator rejects upgrades that introduce non-backwards-compatible value changes without explicit opt-in flag and surfaces a readable diff in the console
Runbook steps reproduced in a staging environment and stakeholder sign-off from Support and SRE
Customer-facing postmortem template and pre-written communications available in Support playbook

postmortem_notes: Immediate cause: race between Helm post-upgrade hooks and operator reconcile loop leading to partially-applied values in tenant CRs
Contributing factors: insufficient preflight checks for non-destructive value changes; lack of tenant-scoped manifest hashing and snapshotting before upgrades
Action items: implement snapshot-fallback, strengthen Helm preflight, add canary-by-namespace rollout, retention policy for snapshots, long-term idempotency fixes
qa_plan: Create synthetic multi-tenant clusters with varying API server latency profiles
Run staged upgrade harness that triggers post-upgrade hooks concurrently with nodeagent reconciliation
Assert quarantined tenants are auto-restored via snapshot-fallback and traffic returns to healthy state within SLO
Verify preflight rejection messages are surfaced in console and API responses
notes_for_oncall: If you see 'tenant.quarantine.triggered' alert: follow playbook at mitigation_playbook_link, attempt manual snapshot-restore if automated fallback fails
Do not perform a full operator rollback unless Playbook authorizes: it can create additional drift across tenants
Contact engineering lead Liam Chen and Support lead Zoe Kim for customer escalations requiring manual intervention
